p2.original: 治疗心理障碍的方法多种多样，但它们都涉及侧重于改善一个人的心理、行为或社会功能的治疗关系。
p2.en: The treatment of mental disorders is varied, but they all involve therapeutic relationships focused on improving a person's psychological, behavioural or social functioning.

p3.original: 当想到“疗法”一词时，你的脑海中很可能会浮现出一个从无数动画片和电影中看到的刻板印象：“神经质”的患者躺在沙发上，长着大胡子的治疗师坐在患者头部的旁边，字迹潦草地记着笔记，同时还做着解释。实际上，这一幕来自经典的弗洛伊德式精神分析，尽管它在20世纪上半叶占据了主导地位，但今天已不多见了。
p3.en: When you think about the word “therapy”, you're likely to have the stereotype of a patient with a large beard sitting next to the patient's head, writing notes and explaining it, as he appears from numerous animations and films. Indeed, this scene, which comes from the classic Freudian psychoanalytical, is rare today, despite its dominance in the first half of the twentieth century.

p4.original: 事实上，现代的心理治疗与关于它的旧的刻板印象存在诸多方面的不同。
p4.en: In fact, modern psychotherapy differs in many ways from its old stereotypes.

p5.original: 第一，大多数治疗师不再让患者（或来访者）躺在沙发上。
p5.en: First, most therapists no longer allow patients (or visitors) to lie on couches.

p6.original: 第二，除了患上DSM-5诊断体系中的那些严重障碍外，人们还针对存在的各种问题寻求治疗：咨询师或治疗师也会帮你做出一些困难的选择，以应对那些学业问题，以及处理丧失或不愉快的人际关系。
p6.en: Secondly, in addition to the serious obstacles in the DSM-5 diagnostic system, people seek treatment for the problems that exist: counsellors or therapists help you to make difficult choices to deal with academic problems and with lost or unhappy relationships.

p7.original: 第三，目前还普遍存在一种对治疗的错误认识，即某些形式的疗法不仅有谈话和解释，涉及的行动也很多，你很快就会注意到这一点。
p7.en: Thirdly, there is also a widespread misconception about treatment, that some forms of therapy have not only talks and explanations, but also a great deal of action, and you will soon notice that.

p8.original: 起初，治疗方法清单似乎提供了一张令人困惑的选项列表。但是你会看到有一条主线贯穿其中，正如我们的核心概念所提示的那样：
p8.en: Initially, the list of treatments seemed to provide a confusing list of options. But you'll see that there's a lead line running through it, as our core concept suggests:

p9.original: 治疗心理障碍的方法多种多样，但它们都涉及侧重于改善一个人的心理、行为或社会功能的治疗关系。
p9.en: The treatment of mental disorders is varied, but they all involve therapeutic relationships focused on improving a person's psychological, behavioural or social functioning.

p10.original: 我们先了解接受治疗的人员的多样性以及在治疗过程中他们会遇到哪些问题，并为探索这些疗法奠定基础。
p10.en: Let us first understand the diversity of people receiving treatment and the problems they will encounter in the process of treatment and lay the foundation for exploring those treatments.

p12.original: 13.1 列出疗法有哪些基本组成部分，并提出运用该治疗方法的专业人员以及接受治疗的人员类型。
p12.en: 13.1 List the basic components of the treatment and indicate the professionals who use it and the types of people who receive it.

p13.original: 13.2 描述在不同的文化中，随着时间的推移如何进行治疗。
p13.en: 13.2 Describe how treatment is administered over time in different cultures.

p16.original: 列出疗法有哪些基本组成部分，并提出运用该治疗方法的专业人员以及接受治疗的人员类型。
p16.en: List the basic components of the treatment and indicate the professionals who use it and the types of persons who receive it.

p17.original: 你为什么要接受治疗？为什么任何人都可能要接受治疗？
p17.en: Why are you being treated? Why can anyone be treated?

p18.original: 人们通常会在遇到无法自行解决的问题时寻求治疗。他们可能会主动寻求治疗，或者家人、朋友、医生或同事建议他们寻求治疗。
p18.en: People usually seek treatment when they encounter problems that cannot be solved on their own. They may seek treatment on their own initiative or be advised by family, friends, doctors or colleagues to seek treatment.

p19.original: 显然，接受治疗并不是说你就是“疯子”。但是你可能被称为“患者”或“来访者”。采取生物学或医学模型治疗的从业人员通常使用“患者”一词，而“来访者”通常是心理学专业人员的用词，他们将心理障碍看作生活问题，而非精神障碍（Rogers，1951；Szasz，1961）。
p19.en: Clearly, treatment does not mean that you are a “crazy”. But you might be called a "patient" or a "visitor." Practitioners who use biological or medical models usually use the term “patient”, whereas “visitor” is usually used by psychological professionals who view mental disorders as a problem of life rather than a mental disorder (Rogers, 1951); Szasz, 1961.

p20.original: 能否获得治疗取决于几个因素。有钱或有足够的医疗保险的人可以很容易就获得治疗。对于穷人来说，特别是贫穷的少数族裔，经济上的匮乏常常会阻碍他们获得专业的精神保健服务（Nemecek，1999；U.S. Department of Health and Human Services，2001）。在许多社区中，缺乏合格的治疗师也可能会使获得治疗受限。身体健康出现问题比心理出现问题更容易得到帮助。有时，心理问题的性质也会影响人们获得帮助的可能性，如患有广场恐怖症的人会发现很难甚至根本无法出门寻求治疗。同样，存在偏执症状的人可能不会去寻求帮助，因为他们根本不相信心理健康专业人员。显然，要让所有需要治疗的人获得帮助，依然面临很多困难。
p20.en: Access to treatment depends on several factors. Treatment is easily available to those who have the money or health insurance. For the poor, especially the poor ethnic minorities, economic deprivation often prevents them from accessing professional mental health services (Nemecek, 1999); U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, 2001. In many communities, the lack of qualified therapists may also limit access to treatment. Problems in physical health are easier to help than problems in mental health. Sometimes the nature of psychological problems also affects the possibility of people getting help, such as those suffering from plaza terror, who find it difficult, if not impossible, to go out for treatment. Similarly, people with paranoid symptoms may not seek help because they do not trust mental health professionals at all. Clearly, there are still many difficulties in reaching all those in need of treatment.

p22.original: 有时，你只需要向有同理心的朋友和家人说说自己的问题，或者你只是为了“听听自己的想法。”但是朋友和家人不仅缺乏如何处理这类复杂精神问题的训练，而且有时他们自己的需求和处事流程可能会对你产生干扰。实际上，他们有时可能就是问题的一部分。正是基于这些原因，我们有必要寻求接受过专业培训的治疗师的帮助。除治疗师的能力外，还有保密问题：如果你希望对自己的问题和顾虑保密，就需要寻求专业的帮助。在所有这些方面，你与治疗师的专业关系不同于友情或亲情。
p22.en: Sometimes you just have to tell your friends and family your problems, or you just want to listen to your own thoughts. But not only do friends and family lack training to deal with such complex mental problems, but they may sometimes interfere with their own needs and processes. In fact, they may sometimes be part of the problem. It is for these reasons that we need to seek the help of a professionally trained therapist. In addition to the capacity of the therapist, there is the issue of confidentiality: if you wish to keep your questions and concerns confidential, you need to seek professional help. In all these respects, your professional relationship with the therapist is different from friendship or kinship.

p23.original: 13.1.2 治疗的组成部分是什么
p23.en: 13.1.2 What are the components of the treatment?

p24.original: 正如我们在核心概念中所表明的那样，几乎在所有形式的治疗中，治疗师与来访者之间都存在某种关系或治疗同盟（therapeutic alliance）。实际上，对治疗效果影响最大的因素就是治疗同盟的质量（Wampold & Brown，2005）。然而，我们必须承认在实验性的计算机治疗程序中，与来访者互动的不是人，而是计算机编程开发的模拟治疗师，“关系”这个概念在这里开始有了拓展。
p24.en: As we have indicated in the core concept, there is a relationship or therapeutic alliance between therapists and visitors in almost all forms of treatment. In fact, the most important factor affecting the effectiveness of treatment is the quality of the therapeutic alliance (Wampold & Brown, 2005). However, we must acknowledge that the concept of “relationship” has begun to expand in experimental computer therapy processes, where visitors are not interacting with human beings, but rather with analog therapists developed by computer programming.

p25.original: 根据你的观点，什么才是良好的治疗同盟？
p25.en: In your opinion, what's a good therapeutic alliance?

p26.original: 你和你的治疗师必须能够作为同盟站在一起，朝着共同的目标，齐心协力应对并解决你的问题（Horvath & Luborsky，1993；Novotney，2013）。为此，信任和同理心是两个基本要素。同时，随着临床医生越来越意识到来访者在性别和种族方面存在多样性，有研究表明，最有效的治疗师是那些可以在来访者自己的文化、经验和母语背景下与他们建立联系的人（Griner & Smith，2006）。
p26.en: You and your therapists must be able to stand together as allies and work together to address and solve your problems in a common goal (Horvath & Luborsky, 1993; Novotney, 2013. To that end, trust and common sense are two essential elements. At the same time, as clinical doctors become more aware of the diversity of visitors in terms of gender and ethnicity, research has shown that the most effective therapists are those who can connect them in their own culture, experience and mother tongue (Griner & Smith, 2006).

p27.original: 治疗过程除了涉及治疗师和来访者之间的关系外，通常还包括以下步骤。
p27.en: The treatment process usually includes the following steps, in addition to the relationship between the therapist and the visitor.

p28.original: 1. 识别问题。这一步意味着双方对一个需要改变的情况或感受的简单描述达成一致，或者一个符合DSM-5的疾病案例，在这一步，治疗师通常会给出哪里出现问题的正式诊断。
p28.en: 1. Identification issues. This step implies agreement on a simple description of a situation or feeling that needs to be changed, or on a case of a disease that fits the DSM-5, at which the therapist usually gives a formal diagnosis of where the problem arises.

p29.original: 2. 找到问题的原因或致使问题一直存在的条件。在某些形式的治疗中，涉及探询过去，尤其是童年时期的经历，寻找患者或来访者不适的根源。或者也有一些治疗方法强调关注当下的病因，即致使问题一直存在的条件。
p29.en: Find the cause of the problem or the conditions that perpetuate it. In some forms of treatment, it involves exploring past experiences, especially in childhood, and finding the root causes of discomfort for patients or visitors. Or there are treatments that highlight the current causes of the disease, that is, the conditions that perpetuate the problem.

p30.original: 3. 决定并实施某种形式的治疗。在这一步，治疗师需要选择某种特定的疗法来最小化或消除困扰症状。最终的治疗取决于问题的性质、治疗师的治疗取向及其接受过的训练。
p30.en: 3. Decide and implement some form of treatment. At this stage, the therapist needs to select a particular treatment to minimize or eliminate the symptoms of distress. The final treatment depends on the nature of the problem, the treatment orientation of the therapist and the training received.

p32.original: 尽管现在寻求治疗的人比过去多，但他们通常是在自己的心理问题变得严重或持续较长时间后才这样做。他们通常会求助于以下七种主要类型的专业人员：咨询心理学家、临床心理学家、精神科医生、精神分析师、精神科执业护士、临床（精神科）社会工作者或牧师。
p32.en: Although more people are now seeking treatment than in the past, they usually do so only after their own psychological problems have become serious or have lasted longer. They usually resort to seven main types of professionals: consulting psychologists, clinical psychologists, psychiatrists, psychoanalysts, psychiatrists, nurses, clinical (psychiatric) social workers or priests.

p33.original: 这些专业人员之间的差异在表13-1中做了重点说明。查看此表时，请注意每种职业类型都有其自己的专业领域。例如，在美国的大多数州，取得药物处方权的专业人员只有医生（包括精神科医生）和精神科执业护士。
p33.en: The differences between these professionals are highlighted in table 13-1. When looking at this table, please note that each occupational category has its own area of specialization. For example, in most states of the United States, only doctors (including psychiatrists) and psychiatric nurses are the professionals who obtain prescriptions for drugs.

p34.original: 目前，临床心理学家正通过他们所在的专业组织寻求获得处方权（Sternberg，2003）。实际上，美国新墨西哥州和路易斯安那州现在已经向完成严格的课程学习计划和实习期间受到监督的心理学家授予处方权（Dittmann，2003）。美国的其他十几个州也出台了类似的法律。同时，美国军方也已经接受了心理学家具有处方权的事实（Dittmann，2004）。然而，这个问题仍然是高度政治化的，特别是受到了医学界的质疑（Fox et al.，2009）。甚至有些临床心理学家也反对处方权，他们担心心理学家会“出卖自己的灵魂”来为寻求药物治疗的公众服务。美国心理学会（APA）前主席乔治·阿尔比（George Albee，2006）曾提及：
p34.en: Currently, clinical psychologists are seeking prescription rights through their professional organisations (Sternberg, 2003). Indeed, the states of New Mexico and Louisiana now grant prescription powers to psychologists supervised during the completion of rigorous curriculum programmes and internships (Dittmann, 2003). Similar laws have been introduced in a dozen other states in the United States. At the same time, the United States military has accepted the fact that psychologists have prescription powers (Dittmann, 2004). However, the issue remains highly politicized, particularly by the medical community (Fox et al., 2009). Even clinical psychologists are opposed to prescription rights and fear that psychologists “sell their own souls” to serve the public seeking medication. George Albee, former President of the American Psychological Association (APA), mentioned:

p35.original: 目前，执业者在实践中成为药物处方者的动机往往与谋生息息相关。社会上流传着这样一种谬论，即精神或情感障碍都是源于大脑的疾病，必须接受药物治疗。心理执业者想要生存的唯一方法是接受这种无稽之谈。
p35.en: At present, the motivation of practitioners to become prescription drug suppliers in practice is often linked to livelihood. Socially there is a myth that mental or emotional disorders are diseases of the brain and must be treated with medication. The only way for psychological practitioners to survive is to accept this nonsense.

p36.original: 无论你是否同意阿尔比的观点，接受过适当培训的心理学家获得处方权的时代已经来临。它将如何改变心理学的面貌还有待观察。
p36.en: Whether or not you agree with Albi, the time has come for appropriately trained psychologists to acquire prescription power. It remains to be seen how it will change the face of psychology.

p37.original: 表13-1 精神卫生专业人员的类型
p37.en: Table 13-1 Types of mental health professionals

p38.original: 13.2 历史和文化背景下的治疗
p38.en: 13.2 Treatment in Historical and Cultural Context

p40.original: 描述在不同的文化中，随着时间的推移如何进行治疗。
p40.en: Describe how treatment is administered over time in different cultures.

p41.original: 我们如何治疗精神障碍取决于我们对精神障碍的看法。例如，如果我们认为精神问题是疾病，那我们采取的方法就会有别于那些相信精神问题是由于人格缺陷或恶魔附体的人。
p41.en: How we treat mental disorders depends on our perception of mental disorders. For example, if we believe that the mental problem is a disease, then the approach we take is different from that of those who believe that the mental problem is due to a personality defect or demonic possession.

p42.original: 任何一个社会对待精神障碍的方式总是取决于其普遍存在的信念。
p42.en: The way in which any society treats mental disorders depends on its prevailing beliefs.

p44.original: 在中世纪的欧洲，人们认为精神障碍由魔鬼和恶魔所致。在这种情况下，“治疗师”的工作就是驱魔或者“打败魔鬼”——使身体成为精神或恶魔不适宜居住的地方。另一种说法则是，精神障碍患者被称为“疯子”，因为依据民间的说法，月亮（拉丁语中的luna）导致了他们发疯。在美国独立战争期间，一些改革者则采取了相对开明的观点，他们敦促精神障碍患者应被安置在“庇护所”中，这样可以使得这些患者免受外界压力的伤害。事实上，几个世纪前就有精神庇护所（Elzamzamy & Patel，2015；Ricardo，2011）。在这种情况下，许多患者的状况得以改善，但不幸的是，“精神庇护所”的理想并非总能实现。
p44.en: In medieval Europe, mental disorders are perceived to be caused by demons and demons. In such cases, the work of a “therapist” is exorcising or “defeating the devil” — making the body a place where the spirit or demons are not fit to live. In another case, persons with mental disorders are referred to as “crazy” because, according to the popular version, the moon (luna in Latin) leads to their madness. During the American War of Independence, some reformers took a relatively enlightened view, urging people with mental disorders to be placed in “shelter” so that they could be protected from external pressure. In fact, there was a spiritual shelter centuries ago (Elzamzamy & Patel, 2015); Ricardo, 2011. In this context, the situation of many patients has improved, but unfortunately the idea of “psychiatric shelter” has not always been achieved.

p45.original: 伦敦的伯利恒医院（Bethlehem Hospital）是最臭名昭著的庇护所，也是首批庇护所之一。在那里观光者只要花几便士，就可以在周末看到精神病患者为他们提供的狂乱和嘈杂的“表演”。结果，“Bedlam”一词（“伯利恒”的缩写）变成描述嘈杂、混乱地方的专用词。
p45.en: Bethlehem Hospital in London (Bethlehem Hospital) was one of the most notorious shelters and one of the first. Tourists there spend a few pence and can see the hysteria and loud “dramas” that mental patients offer them on weekends. As a result, the term “Bedlam” (“Bethlehem”) has become a term used to describe a noisy and chaotic place.

p46.original: 尽管一开始庇护所运动的初衷很好，但由于腐败的政客耗尽了资源，使得状况恶化，最终导致了大多数庇护者只能接受一些看护服务。最糟糕的是，不少人受到了残酷的监禁。例如，看护人员把他们关在笼子里或用铁链拴住他们，或者让他们穿上显示如“伯利恒”字样的衣服。一些人甚至遭到了殴打，以及其他形式的虐待。不难猜测，庇护所里这种歪曲的“治疗”很难让患有心理障碍的人的状况得到改善。
p46.en: Despite the good intentions of the shelter movement at first, the situation worsened by the depletion of resources by corrupt politicians, which eventually led to the majority of asylum-seekers being left with some care services. Worst of all, many have been brutally imprisoned. For example, the caregiver kept them in cages or chained them up, or made them wear clothes that appeared to be “Bethlehem”. Some were even beaten and other forms of ill-treatment. It is not difficult to assume that such distorted “treatment” in the shelter makes it difficult to improve the situation of persons with mental disabilities.

p48.original: 现代的精神卫生专业人员已经摈弃了旧的恶魔模式和完全被滥用的庇护所治疗，而更赞同基于心智和行为的心理学和生物学的疗法。但是，我们也需要看到，由于当前专业人员对心理障碍的病因尚没有形成一致的看法，所以，最合适的治疗是需要我们在众多疗法中进行选择的一门艺术。为了更好地帮助你了解各种疗法，在这里我们先进行一下预览。
p48.en: Modern mental health professionals have abandoned old demon models and completely abused shelter treatment, favouring psychological and biological therapy based on mental and behavioural behaviour. However, we also need to see that, since current professionals do not yet have a common view of the causes of mental disorders, the most appropriate treatment is an art that requires us to choose among the many therapies. In order to help you better understand the various therapies, we'll take a preview here.

p49.original: 心理学取向的治疗常常被简单地称为心理治疗[1]（psychological therapy）。主要强调用心理学技术（而非生物医学干预）来改善杂乱无章的思维、感受及行为。它主要有两种形式。
p49.en: Psychologically oriented treatment is often simply referred to as psychotherapy [1] (psychological therapy). The main emphasis is on psychological techniques (rather than biomedical interventions) to improve disorderly thinking, feeling and behaviour. It takes two main forms.

p50.original: 一种叫作领悟疗法，聚焦于帮助人们理解他们的问题并改变他们的想法、动机或感受。
p50.en: A form of what is known as epithetic therapy focuses on helping people understand their problems and changing their thoughts, motivations or feelings.

p51.original: 另一种称为行为疗法，主要聚焦在行为改变上。实际上，许多心理治疗师把这二者结合起来使用，称为认知行为疗法。
p51.en: Another is called behavioural therapy, which focuses mainly on behavioural change. In fact, many psychotherapists combine the two, known as cognitive behaviour therapy.

p52.original: 相反，生物医学疗法（biomedical therapy）治疗的核心在于通过使用多种药物，包括抗抑郁药、镇静剂和兴奋剂，来改变大脑的基础生物因素并以此解决精神问题。有时可以直接用电磁刺激甚至是手术来治疗大脑。一些医学取向的治疗师也会把药物和心理治疗结合起来使用。
p52.en: On the contrary, the core of biomedical therapy is to change the underlying biological factors of the brain and thus address mental problems through the use of multiple drugs, including antidepressants, sedatives and stimulants. Sometimes the brain can be treated directly with electromagnetic irritation or even surgery. Some medically oriented therapists also use drugs and psychotherapy in combination.

p53.original: 13.2.3 文化背景下的障碍与治疗
p53.en: 13.2.3 Barriers and Treatment in Cultural Contexts

p54.original: 思考和治疗精神障碍的方法存在很大的跨文化差异（Matsumoto，1996）。在西方个人主义文化背景下（即在欧洲和北美），人们普遍认为心理障碍往往是由遗传异常、思维扭曲、不健康的环境或应激源所导致的。但在集体主义文化背景下的人们往往具有不同的看法（Triandis，1990；Zaman，1992）。亚洲社会可能会将心理障碍视为个体与群体之间的脱节。同样，许多非洲人认为，当一个人与自然和生活的社区（包括传承祖先精神的社区）疏远时，就会出现精神障碍（Nobles，1976；Sow，1977）。
p54.en: There are significant intercultural differences in the way mental disorders are thought and treated (Matsumoto, 1996). In the context of Western individualistic cultures (i.e. Europe and North America), it is widely accepted that mental disorders are often caused by genetic anomalies, distortions, unhealthy environments or stressors. However, people tend to have different views in the context of a collectiveist culture (Triandis, 1990); Zaman, 1992. Asian societies may view mental disorders as a disconnect between individuals and groups. Similarly, many Africans believe that when a person is alienated from the community of nature and life, including the community of ancestral spirituality, there is a mental disorder (Nobles, 1976); Sow, 1977.

p55.original: 在这样的文化中，脱离精神障碍患者生活的社区来考虑治疗是无法想象的。相反，康复强调要在一定的社会情境中开展，注重当事人的信仰、家庭、工作和生活环境。非洲人在治疗中使用团体支持的方式，并发展出一种被称为“网络疗法”的方法，在患者的整个人际网络中，亲戚、同事和朋友都将参与治疗（Lambo，1978）。这样的治疗可能还会涉及传统的巫师与受过现代心理学和精神病学培训的精神卫生专业人员共同合作。
p55.en: In such a culture, it is inconceivable that treatment should be considered in communities that live away from people with mental disabilities. Instead, rehabilitation emphasizes the social context in which it takes place, focusing on the beliefs, family, work and living environment of the person concerned. Africans use group-supported approaches to treatment and have developed an approach known as “network therapy”, in which relatives, colleagues and friends are involved throughout the patient's network (Lambo, 1978). Such treatment may also involve traditional witches working with mental health professionals trained in modern psychology and psychiatry.

p56.original: 如果德里克生活在这样的文化中，那么毫无疑问，他会接受巫师的治疗，而这些巫师被认为具有特殊的神秘力量。这类治疗过程会涉及一些仪式，这些仪式把情绪体验和意义感带入治疗的过程。这些仪式将个体患者、巫师和社会与超自然力量联系在一起，最终战胜疯狂（Devereux，1981；Wallace，1959）。
p56.en: If Derek lived in such a culture, there was no doubt that he would be treated by witches, who were considered to be of special mysterious strength. Such treatment involves rituals that bring emotional experience and sense of meaning into the process. These rituals link individual patients, witches and societies to supernatural forces and eventually overcome madness (Devereux, 1981); Wallace, 1959.

p57.original: 西非人对人格和精神障碍的观点 塞内加尔的精神病学家I.索乌（I. Sow）提出了一种人格与精神障碍模型，该模型反映了西非国家对人的内在本质、在社会中的根植以及人与精神性联结的看法（Berry et al.，1992；Sow，1977）。索乌的概念模型描绘了人格的四个层次。塞内加尔人认为，外部的两个层次是人类与其他动物共享的（见图13-1）。最外层是由身体组成的，接下来的两层则包含生命能量。精神或灵魂存在于最深处，即人格的核心。按照这种观点，除了核心外，其他一切都会在个体死亡后消失。
p57.en: The perspective of West Africans on personality and mental disorders. The psychiatrist I. Sow of Senegal proposed a model of personality and mental disorders that reflects the views of West African countries on the intrinsic nature of the human person, its roots in society and the connection between human beings and mentalities (Berry et al., 1992); Sow, 1977. Sow's conceptual model depicts four levels of personality. Senegalese believe that two levels of the external environment are shared between human beings and other animals (see figure 13-1). The outermost layer is made up of the body, and the next two layers contain life energy. The spirit or soul exists at the deepest, the core of the human personality. According to this view, everything else, except the core, disappears after an individual dies.

p58.original: 图13-1 西非国家的精神卫生和精神障碍
p58.en: Figure 13-1 Mental health and mental disorders in West African countries

p59.original: 注：西非人视角下的个人。
p59.en: Note: Individuals from a West African perspective.

p60.original: 当然，非洲文化多种多样。如果用索乌的模型解释所有文化背景下的人格，那一定是错误的。总体来说，它最能代表的是居住在西非塞内加尔土著人民的传统看法。
p60.en: Of course, African cultures are diverse. It would be wrong to use Sow's model to explain the personality in all cultural contexts. In general, it is most representative of the traditional views of the indigenous peoples living in Senegal, West Africa.

p61.original: 在塞内加尔人的信仰体系中，人格的每个内在层面都与自己所属的领域有着互动，就如同身体与所处的物理环境存在各种各样所在交互。第二层连接着社区，第三层连接的则是个人所在的家庭。每个个体的精神内核都与祖先的精神世界联系在一起。由于精神与身体不同，所以当一个人处于睡眠和恍惚状态时，精神就会游离于身体之外，而当身体死亡时，一个人的精神就会永久地离开并与祖先的精神汇聚在一起。
p61.en: In the Senegalese faith system, every internal dimension of the human personality interacts with its own sphere, as does the physical and physical environment in which it interacts in a variety of ways. The second level connects the community, and the third level connects the family where the individual lives. Each individual's inner core is linked to the spiritual world of his ancestors. Because of the difference in mind and body, when a person is in a state of sleep and discomfort, the spirit is removed from the body, and when a body dies, the spirit of a person is permanently removed and congregates with the spirit of his ancestors.

p62.original: 索乌认为，西非人的这种观点可以帮助我们理解非洲人对疾病以及精神障碍的看法。当发生的一些事情干扰到一个人与家庭、社区或者祖先的联结时，他们就会得病。最严重的疾病是与精神世界的交流中断了。而最好的治疗，就是在当事人处于恍惚状态下由治疗师（巫师）给予的精神治疗。
p62.en: Sow believes that this view of West Africans can help us understand Africans' perceptions of disease and mental disorders. When something happens that interferes with a person's connection to a family, community or ancestors, they get sick. The most serious disease is the interruption of communication with the spiritual world. The best treatment is the psychiatric treatment given by the therapist (the witch) in a state of discomfort.

p63.original: 在欧美世界所称的精神障碍，如抑郁症或精神分裂症，在西非人眼里是由那些人格第三层与周围社群连接出现了状况所引起的。我们通常采用心理治疗和药物来治疗精神障碍，但是塞内加尔巫师通过祈祷来治疗这种状况，并以此来解决内在的人际冲突。并且如果他们认为巫术破坏了人格的第二层与大家庭的交流，导致出现了危及生命的身体疾病，那么治疗就需要采用某种仪式以抵消被施予的咒语。与现代心理学所获得的结果一样，索乌建议：有些治疗是成功的，有些治疗是失败的。他将成功归因于每种文化在其自身的治疗形式与被治疗者的信仰体系之间的联系。
p63.en: Mental disorders, such as depression or schizophrenia, are known in the European and American world as being caused in West African eyes by the emergence of connections between the third layer of the human personality and the surrounding communities. Psychotherapy and medication are usually used to treat mental disorders, but Senegalese witches are praying to treat the situation and thus to resolve inherent interpersonal conflicts. And if they believe that witchcraft undermines communication between the second layer of the human personality and the extended family, leading to life-threatening physical diseases, then the treatment requires some ritual to offset the spell imposed. Like the results of modern psychology, Sow recommended that some treatments were successful and some failed. He attributed success to the link between each culture in its own form of treatment and the belief system of the treated.

p64.original: 心理学很有用 准专业人员也能做治疗
p64.en: Psychology works, and paraprofessionals can do therapy.

p65.original: 最好的治疗是否总是需要拥有心理咨询或心理治疗硕士或博士学位，并且训练有素（且昂贵）的专业人员？
p65.en: Does the best treatment always require a master's or doctorate degree in psychological counselling or therapy and a well-trained (and expensive) professional?

p66.original: 还是准专业人员（paraprofessional）就能成为有效的治疗师？
p66.en: Or is paraprosocial to be an effective therapist?

p67.original: 如果你正在寻求治疗，这些问题就显得很重要，因为医院、诊所和其他机构会越来越多地雇用准专业人员来作为节约成本的方式：雇用这些准专业人员所需的费用仅仅占那些有专业资质人员费用的几分之一，他们常被称为“助手”或“咨询师”（尽管许多咨询师拥有专业资质）。
p67.en: If you are seeking treatment, these issues are important because hospitals, clinics and other institutions are increasingly hiring paraprofessionals as a way of saving costs: the cost of employing these paraprofessionals is only a fraction of the cost of those with professional qualifications, often referred to as “assistes” or “consultants” (although many consultants have professional qualifications).

p68.original: 不过令人惊讶的是，文献回顾发现，面对不同的心理问题，两组之间的疗效并没有实质性的差异（Christensen & Jacobson，1994）。从某种意义上说，这是个好消息，因为大众对心理卫生服务的需求远远超过了能够提供帮助的职业治疗师的数量。由于准专业人员可以有效地提供治疗，那些受过良好培训的专业人员就可以腾出时间担任其他工作，如疾病预防和社区教育计划、患者评估、对准专业人员的训练和督导以及研究工作。当然，对于上述结果的解释要特别谨慎，因为专业人员和准专业人员仅仅在领悟疗法上显示出相同的效能，随后我们还将讨论这种疗法（Christensen & Jacobson，1994；Zilbergeld，1986）。这一差异在使用行为疗法的领域还没有得到验证，行为疗法领域需要有关操作性条件反射、经典条件反射以及社会学习理论的知识。
p68.en: It is surprising, however, that the literature reviews found that there is no substantial difference in the efficacy of the two groups in the face of different psychological problems (Christensen & Jacobson, 1994). This is good news in a sense, because the demand for mental health services by the general public far exceeds the number of occupational therapists who can help. Since paraprofessionals can effectively provide treatment, well-trained professionals can be free to take up other tasks such as disease prevention and community education programmes, patient assessment, training and supervision of paraprofessionals, and research. Of course, the above results should be interpreted with particular caution, as professionals and paraprofessionals only show the same effectiveness in epithetology, which we will then discuss (Christensen & Jacobson, 1994); Zilbergeld, 1986. This difference has not yet been validated in the area of behavioural therapy, which requires knowledge of operational retroactivity, classic retroactivity and social learning theory.
